entries.title: Geometries
entries.text: A geometry says where the problem lives: its coordinates, which directions are periodic, where the walls are and what they are called.

entries.title: Spherical shells
entries.text: The space between two concentric spheres, where planets and stars convect: simulations on a CPU or a GPU, rotating convection, discrete adjoints and optimal perturbations, with the same model text as in a box.

entries.title: Channels between two surfaces
entries.text: A channel whose walls are not flat: a wavy bottom, a bump, a corrugated lid.

entries.title: Equations
entries.text: A model is written as on paper: unknowns, parameters, known fields and equations in text, with terms on whichever side you like.

entries.title: Boundary conditions
entries.text: Conditions are declared by boundary name, as on paper; Conatus decides how each one enters the discrete system and prints that decision.

entries.title: Ready problems
entries.text: cn.problems gives canonical flows and model equations ready to solve.

entries.title: Units and conventions
entries.text: Unit systems let you convert between nondimensionalisations with convert(), which checks the supplied unit systems and the scales it needs.

entries.title: Simulations and time steppers
entries.text: A model with dt(...) is integrated by m.simulate(...), with the resolution, the scheme and the time step written in the call.

entries.title: Resolution
entries.text: The resolution report says, for each unknown and each direction, whether the spectral coefficients have decayed, and how many modes a target accuracy would need.

entries.title: GPU
entries.text: The same model runs on an NVIDIA GPU by adding backend="cuda".

entries.title: Diagnostics and visualization
entries.text: Eulerian, Lagrangian and mixing diagnostics computed from the fields of a run, on the CPU or the GPU.

entries.title: Particles and dye of a simulation
entries.text: Tracer particles and a numerical dye that live inside a native simulation: they advance with each step of sim.run, on the CPU or the GPU, and write files in the cn.io layout.

entries.title: Input and output
entries.text: Conatus writes two kinds of HDF5 files.

entries.title: The Studio
entries.text: The Studio shows a running simulation as a film in a browser, and lets you pause, checkpoint, stop or fork it.

entries.title: Pilot a run from a script or an agent
entries.text: Everything the Studio shows about a run, a script can read as JSON, and the commands of the Controls sheet, a script can send (experimental, like the Studio: experimental).

entries.title: Studio limits and timings
entries.text: Every number the Studio, the hub, the relay and the telemetry use on their own is declared in one table, conatus.studio.constants.

entries.title: For AI agents
entries.text: What an AI coding agent reads before using Conatus, and the JSON interface it uses while it works.

entries.title: Notebooks
entries.text: In Jupyter, Conatus objects display as tables and cards.

entries.title: Dynamics
entries.text: Everything Conatus does with a model once it is written: stability, growth, invariant solutions, their branches, their symmetries and their sensitivities.

entries.title: explain() and the Methods paragraph
entries.text: Models, results and solvers describe, in plain text, what they are and which numerical choices they carry.

entries.title: Numerical uncertainty
entries.text: A number computed by a simulation (a growth rate, a mean, a value at a point) depends on the resolution and on the time step.

entries.title: The run registry
entries.text: cn.runs records the computations you may want to find, compare, cite or re-run later, with their numerics, code and machine.

entries.title: Reproducibility and provenance
entries.text: A published number should say which code, which numerics and which machine produced it.

entries.title: Checking an installation
entries.text: python -m conatus doctor says what your machine can run (compiled core, GPU) and, for anything missing, what to do.

entries.title: Errors and what they mean
entries.text: A ConatusError states what is wrong, where (equation, term, variable, group), why the call is refused, and a suggested fix.

entries.title: Experimental features
entries.text: Most of the Conatus API changes only through a declared deprecation.

entries.title: Importing Dedalus scripts
entries.text: cn.from_dedalus(script) builds a Conatus problem from the supported subset of a Dedalus 3 script and reports translated, approximated and unsupported constructs.

entries.title: The expert layer
entries.text: Under every native model there is an explicit problem that you can read, modify or write yourself: bases with their sizes, tau terms, the left and right sides of each equation.

entries.title: IR and operators
entries.text: The expert layer writes problems with Python objects: fields, parameters and operators that build an exact symbolic expression.

entries.title: Bases and domains
entries.text: In the expert layer a domain is a coordinate system with one spectral basis per coordinate, each with its size and dealiasing factor.

entries.title: Tau terms by hand
entries.text: In the expert layer you place the boundary terms yourself; a rank check refuses an ill-posed system before any factorisation.

dynamics.title: Eigenvalues and stability
dynamics.text: Normal modes of a linear problem, each with its backward residual, and the tests that flag or remove spurious modes.

dynamics.title: Onset of convection
dynamics.text: The critical Rayleigh number of Rayleigh–Bénard convection between no-slip walls, and the shape of its mode, in a few calls: from the ready linearization, then from the equations of a normal mode written by hand.

dynamics.title: Non-modal analysis
dynamics.text: Transient growth of a linear operator, measured in the kinetic-energy norm.

dynamics.title: Invariant solutions
dynamics.text: Equilibria, travelling waves and periodic orbits found by Newton–Krylov–hookstep on the flow map of your own time stepper.

dynamics.title: Continuation and bifurcations
dynamics.text: Branches of solutions followed through folds by pseudo-arclength, with branch points, Hopf points, cycles and codimension-two curves located on the way.

dynamics.title: Floquet analysis
dynamics.text: Stability of time-periodic flows by the Hill method: the Floquet exponents are eigenvalues of one large, structured problem.

dynamics.title: Eigenvalues in a region
dynamics.text: The eigenvalues inside a box of the complex plane: how many there are, and which they are.

dynamics.title: Chaos and ensembles
dynamics.text: Lyapunov exponents with error bars, covariant Lyapunov vectors, Poincaré maps, and the fate of many trajectories integrated as one batch.

dynamics.title: Invariant manifolds and slices
dynamics.text: The unstable manifold of an equilibrium as a polynomial parametrization, connections between solutions, and the reduction of a continuous symmetry by a slice.

dynamics.title: Symmetry subspaces
dynamics.text: Computing in an invariant subspace of a symmetry group: fewer unknowns and isolated solutions, at the price of hiding what breaks the symmetry.

dynamics.title: Adjoints and sensitivity
dynamics.text: Tangent and adjoint of the discrete time stepper, adjoint eigenmodes in a declared inner product, the wavemaker and the sensitivity to the base flow.

dynamics.title: Tangent, adjoint and optimal perturbations
dynamics.text: FlowMap is the time-stepping map of a solver, X_0 ↦ X_N, with its discrete tangent (jvp) and adjoint (vjp).

dynamics.title: Data-driven analysis
dynamics.text: Dynamic mode decomposition and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition of snapshots, in a weighted inner product.
